  Quarto scaffold for a humanities article or chapter in the history of
  ideas: interpretive prose, Chicago notes-bibliography, no computed
  statistics.

  CITATIONS. Cite with a *located* key: `[@hobbes1651, p. 91]`. Pandoc
  turns every such citation into a footnote, so do not also type `^[...]`
  around it. Put commentary and the citation in one footnote with
  `^[Compare [@locke1689, bk. 2, §4] on the state of nature.]`. A whole-work
  reference says so: `[@skinner1969, passim]`. `scripts/test_citations.py`
  rejects a citation with no locator.

  QUOTATIONS. Quote in the language you cite. A translation is cited from
  the translation you actually read (`[@hobbes1994, p. 91]`), with the
  original-language passage in the footnote when the argument turns on a
  word. Record the original date in the Zotero `Extra` field
  (`original-date: 1651`) so the bibliography can show it.

  Delete these comments before submission.
-->
